admission.justification: Separating head identity/facts from requirement text prevents duplicate or hidden obligation content across the shared head and form blocks.

applicability: The head and requirement block of fixed sprint/master/task document pages.
conditions: Each fact is drawn only where the document supplies it.
A primary requirement can appear as a head link while its text belongs once to Requirements.

evidence: dashboard/src/panels/detail-panel/page-look.test.tsx: 'leads with the objective, then the labelled facts, then the notes', 'draws the primary requirement as its link and its text once, under Requirements'; the focused set of the reports: 331 passed in 40 files

statement: The head of a task page draws its facts as a strip of labelled facts with the label above the value, and the primary requirement stands there as its link while its text stands once, under Requirements.
